newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BARLOW UPBEAT ON OFFSHORE UNITS' OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: BARLOW UPBEAT ON OFFSHORE UNITS' OUTLOOK.

text.p: Barlow Ltd's offshore operations were well placed for growth as the outlook for the economies in which they operated looked positive after a temporary slowdown, chairman Warren Clewlow said.

"The slowdown in the economies of our main trading partners has proved to be only temporary and a resurgence in economic growth world-wide will cause commodity prices to increase during the coming year," Clewlow said in the group's annual report.
"Following two years of strong recovery our international businesses are well placed for growth and can look to the future with confidence."
Clewlow said an assessment of Barlow's order books and the repositioning of group operations pointed to real earnings growth in the 1996/97 financial year.
"The rate of growth, however, will not be of the same magnitude as that achieved in 1996," he said.
In the year to end September, Barlow reported a 26 percent improvement in attributable profit to 666.9 million rand, boosted by a strong showing from overseas units.
Some 25 percent of attributable profit was earned in foreign currency against 20 percent a year ago.
Clewlow said Barlow experienced both the costs and benefits of South Africa's re-entry into the global economy which was being achieved by ongoing foreign exchange and trade liberalisation.
Costs included stronger competition and higher import prices, but this was offset by the benefits of growing of investment and export opportunities.
